name: IEC bidirectional (universal) shift register
summary: IEC shift register with mode inputs that select shift right, shift left, parallel load or hold.
description: A universal shift register is drawn as an SRG element with two mode-select inputs grouped to produce modes 0 to 3. The clock label shows shift right under one mode and shift left under another, while data inputs are labelled with their mode and control numbers, such as 1,4D for serial right input and 3,4D for parallel load.

These devices are used in data conversion, sequence generation and bidirectional serial links. Reading the compound labels left to right, mode first then clock, tells you exactly when each input is used.
The symbol does not state which mode is safe to change during clocking. Mode changes are normally made with the clock inactive.
readingNotes: Compound labels such as 1,4D give mode then clock.
drawingChecklist: Label both shift directions on the clock.
Label serial and parallel data inputs with their mode numbers.
distinction: A single-direction SRG register has no mode inputs and shifts only one way.
